hero.headline: Six Bodies Recovered From Washington Paper Mill Explosion, Eight Confirmed Dead
hero.body:
Recovery crews have found six of the nine workers missing after an explosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, bringing the total confirmed death toll to eight. Three workers remain unaccounted for at the Nippon mill site.

The disaster occurred when a chemical tank ruptured at the facility. According to reports, eleven people are now presumed dead from the incident, while nine others were injured.

Search and recovery operations continue at the mill as crews work to locate the remaining three missing employees. The explosion site remains an active disaster zone as investigators work to determine the cause of the tank failure.

The Longview paper mill processes pulp and paper products using various chemicals for bleaching and processing operations. These chemicals are typically stored in large industrial containers. The specific chemical involved in the tank rupture has not been identified in available reports.

Families of the missing workers have been waiting for news as recovery efforts proceed. The recovered remains are being transported for identification. Authorities have not released the names of the victims.

The facility has suspended operations following the incident. Industrial accidents involving chemical processing equipment can result from equipment failure, pressure buildup, or structural weaknesses in storage containers.

Local emergency response teams and federal workplace safety investigators are examining the scene. The investigation will focus on the condition of the chemical tank, maintenance records, and safety protocols that were in place at the time of the explosion.

This marks one of the deadliest industrial accidents in Washington state in recent years. The paper industry relies on various chemicals for pulp processing and bleaching operations, which creates inherent hazards in facilities handling these materials.

The three workers who remain missing are still being sought by recovery teams working through the damaged sections of the mill. Recovery efforts continue as authorities work to complete the search of the disaster site.

The community of Longview, a timber and paper industry center along the Columbia River, has been affected by the scale of the tragedy. The incident has prompted significant response from multiple agencies coordinating recovery and investigation efforts.

Support services have been made available to families and coworkers of those killed in the explosion. Emergency services personnel have worked extensively at the site to recover remains and secure the area.

As the investigation proceeds, authorities will examine all factors that may have contributed to the tank rupture. The focus remains on understanding the equipment failure and determining whether any lapses in maintenance or safety protocols played a role in the disaster.

cards.headline: US and Iran Near Deal to Extend Ceasefire and Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran are close to an agreement that would extend a ceasefire and reopen a key shipping lane, though both nations' leaders have yet to approve the framework.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance said the United States and Iran are very close to reaching a deal but have not finalized it yet. US officials confirmed to the BBC that a framework for extending the ceasefire has been agreed upon, though it still requires approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership.

The proposed deal would end the current conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global oil. During cabinet discussions, Trump threatened to "blow up" Oman if it fails to "behave," following reports that Iran and Oman were discussing jointly charging tolls for ships passing through the waterway.

cards.headline: Netanyahu Orders Israeli Forces to Control 70% of Gaza
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israeli military to expand territorial control to 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, a move that threatens to collapse an already fragile ceasefire and worsen humanitarian conditions in the devastated territory.

Under an October ceasefire brokered by the United States, Israeli forces initially withdrew to a demarcation line that gave Israel control of 53 percent of Gaza. Since then, Israeli forces have steadily advanced westward into areas previously controlled by Hamas, establishing an expanding buffer zone where they claim the right to prevent entry and use force against perceived threats.

Speaking at a conference in an occupied West Bank settlement, Netanyahu outlined Israel's territorial goals. "We are currently squeezing Hamas. We now control 60 percent of the territory in the strip. You know, we were at 50, we moved to 60. My directive is to move to 70 percent," he said.

The expansion would violate the October ceasefire agreement, the UN Security Council resolution that endorsed it, and Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan. That plan established a temporary dividing line between Israeli and Hamas-controlled zones pending further negotiations and stated that no Palestinians would be forced to leave Gaza.

Defence Minister Israel Katz said the government's ultimate goal is for large numbers of Palestinians to leave Gaza through what he termed "voluntary migration." Human rights advocates describe this as ethnic cleansing achieved by making conditions intolerable.

Throughout the eight-month ceasefire, Israeli forces have killed more than 900 Palestinians through gunfire and airstrikes in areas under their control or nearby. Israeli-backed armed militias have taken an active role along the ceasefire line, advancing westward and ordering residents to evacuate their homes. One Gaza resident, Wael Nayef Abu al-Ajeen, described being forced out by militiamen who gave his family until 10 p.m. to leave their area near Deir al-Balah.

The expansion would force Gaza's 2.2 million surviving Palestinians into less than a third of their original territory. The area is already described as the single most overcrowded place on the planet, with every available space occupied by displaced families and improvised shelters.

Muhammad Shehada, a visiting fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, said the directive amounts to declaring Trump's peace framework "null and void." Nasser Khdour, a researcher at the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project, noted that militias are not only attacking Hamas but also forcibly displacing residents living near the ceasefire line.

The Israeli army declined to comment on Netanyahu's directive, referring requests to the political leadership. The timeline for implementing the expansion remains unclear.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Ebola-exposed Americans from returning to US
cards.teaser: Americans exposed to Ebola will be quarantined in Kenya rather than allowed to return to the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return home. The 50-bed field hospital will open Friday.

Some experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US could hinder treatment efforts for the outbreak.

cards.headline: US to Open Quarantine Facility in Kenya for Americans Exposed to Ebola
cards.teaser: A temporary medical facility for Americans exposed to Ebola will open in Kenya, as officials decide against bringing patients to the United States for treatment.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The facility is set to begin operations Friday.

The decision has sparked significant criticism both domestically and internationally. Some experts argue that the approach of keeping Americans abroad rather than allowing them to return home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Guatemala Agrees to Joint Drug Gang Operations With U.S.
cards.teaser: Guatemala agreed to conduct joint operations with U.S. forces targeting drug gangs inside Guatemalan borders, expanding the Trump administration's military cooperation in Latin America.
cards.body:
Guatemala has agreed to permit joint military operations with the United States against drug trafficking organizations within its borders. The arrangement allows U.S. forces to conduct strikes alongside Guatemalan military units.

This agreement is part of the Trump administration's broader initiative to secure cooperation from Latin American governments on anti-narcotics operations involving American military personnel operating in their territories.

cards.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Calls for New Relationship With U.S. in New York
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada's distancing from the United States benefits Americans, speaking to an audience in New York.
cards.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech in New York calling for a new partnership between Canada and the United States. He emphasized the need for a "true partnership" that would reimagine economic cooperation in sectors facing global competition challenges.

Carney framed the proposal as beneficial to both nations, suggesting that greater collaboration would help strengthen America's position. The speech signals Canada's interest in deepening ties with its southern neighbor through coordinated economic strategy.

cards.headline: U.S. Officials Report Progress Toward Deal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: American officials say they are closing in on an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though President Trump has not yet approved the framework.
cards.body:
U.S. officials say they are closing in on an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the crucial waterway disrupted since the start of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. A framework for extending the current cease-fire has been agreed upon, pending approval from President Trump and Iran's leadership, according to officials who spoke with the BBC.

The emerging deal could create space for more substantive negotiations between the two nations. However, complications have emerged, including reports of talks between Iran and Oman about jointly charging tolls for ships passing through the strait, which has prompted strong reactions from Trump.

cards.headline: Iran Launches Attack on Kuwait, U.S. Central Command Says
cards.teaser: The U.S. military described an Iranian attack on Kuwait as an egregious ceasefire violation, testing the fragile truce between the two countries.
cards.body:
The U.S. and Iran have exchanged strikes as negotiations continue over a potential ceasefire agreement. American officials are working toward an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which could extend the current ceasefire and lead to broader talks. However, President Trump has not yet approved the emerging framework.

The military escalation comes amid active diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. U.S. officials have indicated they are closing in on terms for a deal, though the recent strikes underscore the tensions between the two countries even as peace discussions advance.

cards.headline: Guatemala Agrees to Joint Drug Gang Operations With U.S.
cards.teaser: Guatemala agreed to conduct joint operations with U.S. forces targeting drug gangs inside Guatemalan borders, expanding the Trump administration's military cooperation in Latin America.

cards.headline: Portugal Records Hottest May Day as Heat Wave Grips Europe
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest May day as a heat wave spread across Europe, with red alerts issued in Italy and students taking exams in overheated schools in France.
cards.body:
Portugal recorded its highest temperature ever measured in May as a heat wave affected multiple European countries. Red weather alerts were issued in Italy warning residents of dangerous conditions, while French students sat for examinations in school buildings lacking adequate cooling.

The extreme temperatures arrived earlier in the year than typical European heat waves. The weather pattern brought unusually high readings across southern Europe, forcing governments to issue health warnings and adjust public activities to protect vulnerable populations from heat-related illness.

cards.headline: Austrian Man Sentenced to 15 Years for Planned Taylor Swift Concert Attack
cards.teaser: A 21-year-old Austrian man received a 15-year prison sentence after being found guilty of plotting to attack a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna.
cards.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been convicted and sentenced to 15 years in prison for planning an attack on a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna. He was found guilty of planning the attack along with other terrorism-related offenses.

Authorities discovered and disrupted the plot before any attack could take place. The case attracted significant international attention given the prominence of the intended target and the large audiences that typically attend Taylor Swift concerts.

cards.headline: Justice Department Opens Criminal Investigation Into E. Jean Carroll
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has launched a criminal probe into E. Jean Carroll, who successfully sued President Trump for defamation and battery.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors are investigating whether E. Jean Carroll made false statements about how she funded her civil lawsuits against Trump. The criminal probe centers on the financing arrangements for her legal representation.

Carroll won two separate civil cases against Trump—one involving battery and defamation claims tied to a decades-old sexual assault allegation, and another for defamation following Trump's public denials of the allegations. The Justice Department is examining the accuracy of Carroll's disclosures regarding financial support she received during the litigation.

cards.headline: US to Open Quarantine Facility in Kenya for Americans Exposed to Ebola
cards.teaser: A temporary medical facility for Americans exposed to Ebola will open in Kenya, as officials decide against bringing patients to the United States for treatment.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The facility is set to begin operations Friday.

The decision has sparked significant criticism both domestically and internationally. Some experts argue that the approach of keeping Americans abroad rather than allowing them to return home may hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Military Officials Did Not Report SAS War Crimes Allegations Over Morale Concerns
cards.teaser: British military officials chose not to refer allegations of extra-judicial killings by SAS troops to police, citing concerns about unit morale, an inquiry heard.
cards.body:
Military officials testified that they withheld allegations of war crimes committed by SAS troops from police investigators due to worries about damaging morale. The decision delayed civilian law enforcement from learning about claims of extra-judicial killings for several years.

The inquiry is examining whether special forces soldiers committed unlawful killings during operations. Military police were kept unaware of the allegations during the period when officials opted against making referrals to civilian authorities.

cards.headline: UK Home Office to Use AI Facial Recognition for Asylum Seeker Age Verification
cards.teaser: Britain will deploy artificial intelligence technology to assess the ages of asylum seekers starting next year, the Home Office announced.
cards.body:
The UK Home Office plans to use AI-powered facial recognition software to verify whether asylum seekers are adults or children. The technology is set to launch next year as part of efforts to identify migrants who misrepresent their ages.

According to the Home Office, the tool aims to catch adult migrants attempting to claim they are minors. Age assessments are a key factor in determining how asylum seekers are housed and processed through the immigration system.

cards.headline: First Rooftop Intensive Care Unit Opens in London
cards.teaser: An outdoor intensive care ward has opened at a London hospital to monitor whether fresh air exposure improves recovery for seriously ill patients.
cards.body:
King's College Hospital in London has opened the first rooftop intensive care ward, bringing critically ill patients into an outdoor medical environment. The facility will monitor whether this approach improves recovery outcomes for seriously ill patients compared to traditional indoor ICU settings.

The experimental ward represents a significant shift in intensive care design, allowing patients exposure to outdoor air and natural light while receiving intensive medical supervision. Medical staff will track patient outcomes to assess what health benefits, if any, result from the outdoor setting.

hero.headline: Dell shares surge 31% after company raises outlook for AI server sales
hero.body:
Dell Technologies shares jumped 31% following the company's announcement of its strongest sales growth since returning to public markets in 2018, along with a significantly raised forecast for artificial intelligence server revenue.

The computer maker increased its projection for AI server sales to $60 billion. During its most recent quarter, AI server revenue grew more than 750%, which helped push the company's second quarter and full-year guidance beyond what Wall Street analysts had anticipated.

This performance represents a major milestone for Dell as it benefits from the accelerating demand for AI infrastructure. Organizations across various sectors are pouring resources into AI computing capabilities, generating substantial demand for specialized servers that can handle machine learning tasks.

Dell's strong results reflect a wider pattern in which technology companies are capitalizing on the rush to build out AI systems. The company has established itself as a critical supplier of the hardware required to power AI applications, competing with other leading server manufacturers for market share in this rapidly growing sector.

The significant stock price increase has added billions to Dell's market value and marks one of the company's largest single-day gains since its return to public trading six years ago. The surge also boosted shares of other technology companies in after-hours trading as investors reassessed the outlook for corporate spending on AI technologies.

Market watchers had closely monitored Dell's AI server business as a measure of broader corporate technology spending trends. The robust results suggest that enterprises continue to commit substantial funds to AI infrastructure despite economic headwinds and uncertainty.

Dell reported first quarter fiscal 2027 results that surpassed Wall Street expectations across multiple categories. The company's traditional PC and enterprise storage divisions also showed strength, though the AI server business generated the most investor interest and enthusiasm.

The stock rally positions Dell among the best-performing technology companies in recent market sessions and validates its strategic direction of prioritizing AI infrastructure as a key growth opportunity.

The company's success underscores how AI development has created unprecedented structural demand for specialized, high-performance computing capacity. Many organizations are struggling to secure the necessary equipment to support their AI initiatives, creating a favorable environment for suppliers like Dell that can deliver the required hardware at scale.

The results also have implications for the broader technology sector, suggesting that corporate investment in AI infrastructure remains strong and continues to drive growth across multiple companies and industries involved in supporting the AI buildout.

cards.headline: Caesars Entertainment sold to Tilman Fertitta for $17.6 billion
cards.teaser: The Las Vegas casino operator agreed to be acquired by billionaire Tilman Fertitta in a deal that could give him control of four Atlantic City casinos.
cards.body:
Caesars Entertainment, a major Las Vegas Strip casino operator, has been sold to Fertitta Entertainment. The deal values the company at approximately $5.7 billion in equity as part of the $17.6 billion transaction.

Tilman Fertitta, who owns the Houston Rockets basketball team, will now control Caesars' extensive portfolio of casino properties. The acquisition significantly expands Fertitta's footprint in the gambling industry.

cards.headline: Federal regulator pauses Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern railroad merger review
cards.teaser: The Surface Transportation Board delayed proceedings on the $71.5 billion merger after accepting a revised application from the two railroad companies.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board accepted a revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but paused the review process. The $71.5 billion deal would create the first transcontinental railroad in the United States.

Union Pacific refuted new claims from state attorneys general, stating it had provided all requested information in its merger paperwork. The federal agency's decision to delay proceedings adds uncertainty to the timeline for completing what would be one of the largest railroad mergers in American history.

cards.headline: Stock market reaches new highs as US and Iran extend ceasefire
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record closing levels after reports of a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations and strong corporate earnings.
cards.body:
US stock indexes climbed to record levels as diplomatic progress emerged between the US and Iran. The framework for a ceasefire extension has been agreed pending approval from both countries' leadership, according to US officials. Oil prices initially spiked on reports of clashes but retreated as news of the diplomatic breakthrough spread.

The market rally was fueled by strong corporate earnings alongside the geopolitical developments. Wall Street pushed to new records, with both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reaching closing highs. Neither the US nor Iran appears interested in returning to full-scale conflict despite recent military exchanges.

cards.headline: IBM commits $5 billion to secure open-source software with AI
cards.teaser: IBM and Red Hat launched a major initiative to use artificial intelligence to combat cybersecurity threats in open-source software.
cards.body:
IBM and Red Hat pledged $5 billion for an AI-driven open-source security initiative. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said the Mythos incident was the critical trigger for the company's cybersecurity push.

The commitment aims to redefine the future of open-source software in the AI era by using artificial intelligence to identify and address security vulnerabilities. IBM described the initiative as an effort to secure the software foundations that underpin much of modern technology infrastructure.

cards.headline: Treasury Department launches Trump Accounts app nationwide
cards.teaser: The federal government released a mobile application to manage $1,000 investment accounts created for each American child.
cards.body:
The US Treasury has rolled out the Trump Accounts app nationwide, a digital platform that allows parents and guardians to manage federal investment accounts for their children. Each child receives $1,000 in government funding through the program.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app's launch, making the application available across the country. The platform enables families to track and manage their federally funded accounts, which are designed to provide financial support for American children.

cards.headline: ABC accuses Trump administration of threatening broadcast licenses
cards.teaser: The television network said the Federal Communications Commission is targeting its station licenses in what it called unconstitutional retaliation.
cards.body:
ABC accused the Trump administration of threatening its broadcast licenses through the Federal Communications Commission. The network called the regulator's actions a campaign of unconstitutional retaliation.

The TV network issued a statement criticizing the FCC for what it described as targeting its station licenses. ABC characterized the regulatory pressure as part of a broader effort to punish the broadcaster, though specific details of the alleged threats were not provided in available reports.

hero.headline: Cloud providers redesign infrastructure for AI-generated traffic
hero.body:
Major cloud infrastructure companies are rebuilding core internet systems to handle machine-generated traffic as artificial intelligence agents move from experimental projects into production environments.

AWS and Cloudflare are among the companies redesigning their infrastructure to accommodate a shift away from human-driven internet usage. The changes reflect expectations that AI agents will become a dominant source of web traffic.

The infrastructure overhaul addresses fundamental differences between how humans and machines access online services. AI agents generate different traffic patterns and make requests at speeds and volumes that differ from traditional human browsing.

Cloud providers are adjusting their systems as companies deploy AI agents for tasks ranging from data retrieval to automated decision-making. These agents operate continuously and make rapid-fire requests to web services and APIs.

The shift comes as businesses move AI capabilities from testing phases into everyday operations. Companies using AI agents need infrastructure that can handle automated processes running at machine speed rather than human pace.

The redesign efforts span multiple layers of internet infrastructure, from content delivery networks to server architecture. Providers are building systems optimized for the request patterns and data flows generated by automated agents rather than individual users clicking through websites.

This represents a fundamental change in how internet infrastructure is designed. For decades, systems were built around the assumption that humans would be the primary users, with design choices reflecting human browsing speeds and patterns.

The transition indicates that AI agents are becoming common enough in production environments to justify wholesale infrastructure changes by major cloud providers. The companies are investing in these redesigns as they anticipate continued growth in machine-to-machine internet traffic.

cards.headline: Developer embeds data-deletion code targeting AI assistants
cards.teaser: A software developer added hidden instructions to open-source code that told AI coding agents to delete application output.
cards.body:
A developer added an undisclosed prompt injection to code in jqwik, an open-source software library. The hidden addition contained instructions directing AI coding agents to delete application output.

The insertion targeted what the developer described as vibe coders, a term referring to programmers who rely heavily on AI assistance. The prompt injection was designed to trigger when AI tools read and processed the code.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas
cards.teaser: New state data shows Waymo holds the largest share of registered self-driving vehicles as Tesla registers fewer units.
cards.body:
A new Texas law established a tracking tool that provides public visibility into autonomous vehicle registrations across the state. The data reveals that Waymo leads competitors in the number of registered robotaxis and self-driving vehicles.

The registration system accounts for both passenger-focused robotaxis and autonomous trucks designed for freight operations. Tesla currently trails behind Waymo in registration numbers.

cards.headline: Language models treat false statements as true despite warnings
cards.teaser: Testing shows AI language models represent false claims as accurate even after receiving explicit warnings about their falsehood.
cards.body:
Fine-tuning tests revealed that large language models persistently treat false statements as factual, even when explicitly warned otherwise. Researchers found that LLMs displayed a consistent bias toward confidently presenting claims as true, regardless of signals indicating the information was incorrect.

This pattern suggests a fundamental challenge in how these models process and represent information. The findings highlight a potential vulnerability in relying on language models for accuracy-critical applications.

cards.headline: Glean reaches $300 million in annual revenue
cards.teaser: The enterprise AI search startup tripled its revenue as budget-cutting became a key sales pitch for customers.
cards.body:
Glean, an enterprise AI search startup, crossed $300 million in annual revenue. The company tripled its revenue over the past year.

The growth occurred as major tech companies entered the enterprise AI search category. Glean has positioned AI-driven budget reduction as a primary selling point to corporate customers.

cards.headline: US healthcare costs remain high with poor health outcomes
cards.teaser: A new study found American healthcare spending stays elevated while producing inferior results compared to peer nations.
cards.body:
Research comparing US healthcare to other developed countries found Americans pay significantly more for medical care while receiving worse health outcomes. The study characterized the spending levels as excessive and the results as inadequate.

The researchers identified strategies that could improve healthcare performance. The study concluded the United States is not implementing these approaches.

cards.headline: Slate Auto to announce electric vehicle pricing in June
cards.teaser: The startup backed by Jeff Bezos will take preorders and reveal final pricing for its EV on June 24.
cards.body:
Slate Auto plans to announce pricing for its electric vehicle and begin accepting preorders on June 24. The startup, which is backed by Jeff Bezos, has not yet revealed the vehicle's cost.

The company expects to begin shipping vehicles to customers by the end of this year.

hero.headline: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup winner whose aggressive playing style made him a feared competitor throughout his NHL career, has died at age 60. According to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to a furniture store showroom in Lake Park, Florida, early Thursday morning where Lemieux was found. The sheriff's office identified the incident as an apparent suicide.

Lemieux's Stanley Cup victories came with three different franchises, a rare accomplishment in professional hockey. His championship rings place him among a select group of players who achieved sustained success across multiple organizations and eras of the sport.

Known for his fierce approach to the game, Lemieux earned a reputation as a hard-hitting winger whose physical style of play frequently frustrated opposing teams. While his combative nature sometimes overshadowed his considerable talent, his ability to perform in crucial playoff moments remained undeniable. He won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1995, awarded annually to the Stanley Cup Finals MVP.

Throughout his career, Lemieux demonstrated an ability to contribute to winning cultures across different team systems and coaching philosophies. His adaptability allowed him to thrive in various roles, making him a valuable asset to championship rosters that featured many of the sport's most talented players.

Beyond his on-ice accomplishments, Lemieux later transitioned into work as a player agent following his retirement from professional hockey. This career move extended his influence within the sport and allowed him to continue shaping the professional landscape.

Lemieux became known by certain nicknames that reflected his confrontational approach to competition. His post-game behavior and regular feuds with opposing players made him a polarizing figure within the hockey community, though his supporters pointed to his passion and competitive spirit as defining characteristics.

The hockey community has lost a player whose achievements represent a level of excellence achieved by few in NHL history. Four Stanley Cup championships, earned across multiple decades of professional play, underscore his sustained contributions to winning teams.

The incident marked a tragic conclusion to the life of a man who left an indelible mark on professional hockey. His passing serves as a reminder of the importance of mental health and support systems within professional sports communities.

Lemieux's legacy extends beyond his championship victories and statistical accomplishments. His fierce competitive nature, whether viewed positively or negatively by observers, made him a memorable figure from an era of intense playoff competition and memorable championship runs.

cards.headline: MLB owners propose salary cap for first time since 1994 strike
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball owners have submitted a collective bargaining proposal that includes a hard salary cap and salary floor.
cards.body:
MLB owners proposed a salary cap system for the first time since the 1994-95 strike that canceled the World Series. The proposal includes both a hard salary cap and a salary floor set at $171 million.

The proposal represents the league's initial offer to the players union in ongoing collective bargaining negotiations. A hard salary cap would fundamentally change baseball's economic structure, which currently operates without a maximum team payroll limit. The inclusion of both a ceiling and floor aims to address competitive balance concerns across the league's franchises.

cards.headline: NBA changes draft lottery system to reduce tanking incentive
cards.teaser: The NBA Board of Governors approved a new draft lottery system designed to discourage teams from losing games intentionally.
cards.body:
The NBA has revamped its draft lottery format after a vote by the Board of Governors. The league expanded the lottery structure to address concerns about teams tanking to improve their draft position.

The new system alters the odds and structure that determine which teams receive the top picks in the annual draft. The changes aim to reduce the competitive advantage teams gain by finishing with poor records. The reform represents a significant shift in how the league allocates its most valuable asset for team building.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi selected for sixth World Cup with Argentina
cards.teaser: The defending champion will be captained by Messi at the 2026 tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi will captain Argentina at the 2026 World Cup, marking his sixth appearance at the tournament. This extends his record for World Cup participation among Argentine players. Argentina will defend its title after winning the previous World Cup with Messi as captain, securing the trophy that had long eluded him.

The 2026 tournament will be hosted jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

cards.headline: Thunder and Spurs play elimination game in Western Conference finals
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City can advance to the NBA Finals with a win in Game 6 against San Antonio.
cards.body:
The Thunder and Spurs are playing Game 6 of the Western Conference finals, with San Antonio facing elimination. Oklahoma City can close out the series and advance to the NBA Finals with a victory.

The Thunder's role players have elevated their performance during the conference finals, contributing at high levels alongside the team's stars. San Antonio must win to force a Game 7 back in Oklahoma City. The series has been closely contested, with both teams trading advantages throughout the playoff matchup.

cards.headline: Luke Littler wins Premier League darts title in close final
cards.teaser: The world champion defeated Luke Humphries 11-10 to regain the Premier League trophy at The O2.
cards.body:
Luke Littler won the Premier League darts title in an epic final at The O2, defeating Luke Humphries 11-10. The world champion produced one of his finest performances to reclaim the Premier League title in what has been described as one of the competition's greatest finals.

After his victory, an emotional Littler revealed he had nearly quit the Premier League during the tournament. Despite the challenges he faced, his performance against Humphries showcased his quality as one of darts' top players.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner eliminated early from French Open
cards.teaser: The top-ranked player's exit opens the men's draw at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has been knocked out of the French Open in the second round, losing to Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerúndolo 3-6, 2-6, 7-5, 6-1, 6-1. Sinner attributed his defeat to illness rather than the extreme heat at Roland Garros, describing the loss as "tough to accept" given his recent form.

With the top seed gone, the men's title race has opened up considerably. Alexander Zverev is now the new favourite for the championship. Sinner plans to skip grass-court tournaments and take time to recover before Wimbledon.

hero.headline: Man Who Planned to Attack Taylor Swift Concert Sentenced to 15 Years
hero.body:
A 21-year-old Austrian man has been found guilty of planning a jihadist attack on Taylor Swift concertgoers in Vienna and sentenced to 15 years in prison. Beran A., identified according to Austrian privacy laws, pleaded guilty to terrorism-related charges connected to the foiled plot.

The defendant admitted to planning an assault on fans gathered outside Ernst Happel stadium during Swift's scheduled performances in August 2024. Authorities estimated up to 30,000 people would have been outside the venue each night, with another 65,000 inside. Prosecutors say Beran A. aimed to "kill as many people as possible" using knives and homemade explosives.

The plot was disrupted at the last minute, leading Austrian authorities to cancel Swift's three scheduled performances. Intelligence from the United States contributed to the decision to scrapped the concerts. When police searched Beran A.'s apartment on August 7, 2024, one day before the first scheduled show, they discovered bomb-making materials.

"Having our Vienna shows cancelled was devastating," Swift said in a statement posted to Instagram two weeks after the cancellation. "The reason for the cancellations filled me with a new sense of fear, and a tremendous amount of guilt because so many people had planned on coming to those shows."

Beran A. had allegedly networked with other Islamic State members before the planned attack. Prosecutors say the group discussed acquiring weapons and manufacturing bombs. Days before the concert, the defendant allegedly attempted to illegally purchase firearms, including a machine gun and hand grenade. He also reportedly viewed Islamic State instructional videos on making shrapnel bombs and produced a small quantity of an explosive compound.

Beyond the Swift concert plot, Beran A. is also accused of planning attacks in the Middle East alongside a Slovak national named Arda K. Prosecutors allege both men traveled to designated cities in March 2024 with intentions to carry out militant attacks. Beran A. traveled to Dubai while Arda K. went to Istanbul. A third man, Hasan E., is believed to have carried out a knife attack at Mecca's Grand Mosque on March 11, 2024, and remains in custody in Saudi Arabia.

Beran A.'s defense attorney, Anna Mair, stated that her client was remorseful. "Of course, he deeply regrets it all," Mair said outside court. "It is also due to the long period of detention that he says it was the biggest mistake of his life."

The case faced comparison to a 2017 suicide bombing at an Ariana Grande concert in Manchester, which killed 22 people. A Berlin court separately convicted a 16-year-old Syrian teenager of contributing to the Taylor Swift concert plot, sentencing him to an 18-month suspended sentence.

cards.headline: Bari Weiss Replaces Executive Producer at 60 Minutes, Two Correspondents Exit
cards.teaser: CBS News leader Bari Weiss replaced the executive producer at 60 Minutes and two correspondents left the program in a major reorganization.
cards.body:
CBS News announced sweeping changes to 60 Minutes, appointing Nick Bilton, a former New York Times tech journalist, as the show's new executive producer. Bilton replaces Tanya Simon, who had held the role since the spring of 2025 following the resignation of longtime producer Bill Owens.

The reorganization comes as correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi exit the program. Vega expressed concerns about the broadcast's future under the leadership changes implemented by CBS parent company Paramount Skydance, citing worries about editorial integrity at the decades-old newsmagazine.

cards.headline: The Commodores Drop Out of Freedom 250 Concerts Following Trump Ties Backlash
cards.teaser: The Commodores withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series in Washington after fans objected to the event's connections to Trump.
cards.body:
The Commodores joined at least four other musical acts in withdrawing from the Freedom 250 concert series, a Trump administration-organized event scheduled for Washington DC's National Mall to commemorate America's 250th anniversary. Morris Day was among the first to exit, calling his initial participation a "baseless rumor" hours after the lineup announcement.

The mass departures occurred just one day after the concert series was announced, as performers responded to public criticism over the event's Trump administration ties.

cards.headline: CBS Says Deal With Byron Allen Will Generate $15 Million in Late-Night Profit
cards.teaser: CBS projects it will earn $15 million in profit by leasing its late-night time slot to Byron Allen instead of producing a traditional show.
cards.body:
CBS said its decision to lease late-night programming time to Byron Allen will generate $15 million in profit. The broadcast network replaced its traditional late-night format with the arrangement after canceling The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

The Paramount Skydance-owned network faced criticism for weeks over the decision to oust Colbert and end the long-running program. CBS executives said leasing the time slot proved more profitable than producing original late-night programming. The move represents a shift in how major broadcast networks approach late-night television.

cards.headline: The White Lotus Films Cannes Closing Night Scene With Laura Dern and Steve Coogan
cards.teaser: Production on The White Lotus Season 4 moved to Cannes, where the show recreated a dramatic closing night scene at the Palais des Festivals.
cards.body:
The fourth season of The White Lotus moved production to Cannes after completing filming at Chateau de la Messardiere in Saint-Tropez. The production took over the Palais des Festivals to shoot what appear to be pivotal scenes for the season.

The cast includes Laura Dern, Steve Coogan, Ari Graynor, and Max Greenfield. The production recreated a dramatic Cannes closing night for the Mike White anthology series. The scenes filmed at the festival venue suggest major plot developments in the Saint-Tropez-set season.

cards.headline: Tito Double P Releases Second Solo Album Acomodo
cards.teaser: The música mexicana star released his second solo album, a 23-track project.
cards.body: The album represents the next step for the performer as a solo artist. Acomodo follows his earlier work and showcases his development within the música mexicana genre.

cards.headline: Jay Wheeler Returns With Album La Voz Favorita
cards.teaser: The Puerto Rican artist released a new album tracing his roots across trap and reggaeton.
cards.body:
Jay Wheeler released La Voz Favorita, an album that explores his musical origins. The Puerto Rican performer traces his roots across trap and reggaeton styles on the project.

Fans call Wheeler Latin music's favorite voice. The new album marks his return after previous releases and demonstrates his range across urban Latin genres.

hero.headline: US and Iran reach tentative 60-day ceasefire extension, nuclear talks framework
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative agreement to extend their ceasefire for 60 days and establish a framework for discussions on Iran's nuclear program, according to US sources. The deal also aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping passage closed by Iran early in the three-month conflict.

President Donald Trump unilaterally announced the ceasefire extension on Tuesday, stating he would hold off military operations until Iranian leaders submit a unified peace proposal. "I have therefore directed our Military to continue the Blockade and remain ready and able, and will therefore extend the Ceasefire until such time as their proposal is submitted," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The move came after intense diplomatic efforts involving Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who has served as a principal mediator between the two countries. However, Iran's response has been mixed and cautious.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and the regime's lead negotiator, dismissed Trump's ceasefire extension as "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike." His adviser, Mahdi Mohammadi, wrote on social media that "the losing side cannot dictate terms" and warned that continuing the US blockade would be met with military response.

The disagreement centers partly on the US Navy blockade of Iranian ports. Iran has demanded the blockade end before negotiations can resume, while Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have stated the blockade will continue. The ongoing blockade threatens to fill Iran's oil storage capacity within days, forcing wells to shut down.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has had severe global consequences. The waterway normally handles about a fifth of the world's oil and gas supplies. Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, described the combined impact of the conflict's effects on oil and Russia's war on gas supplies as "the biggest crisis in history" in global energy markets.

A first round of talks in Islamabad ended 10 days ago without agreement on reopening the strait. Meanwhile, tensions have escalated as the US seized Iranian cargo vessels and boarded an oil tanker previously sanctioned for smuggling Iranian crude.

Despite the tentative agreement's framework, significant disagreements remain. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei characterized recent US actions against vessels as "piracy at sea and state terrorism," questioning Washington's sincerity in negotiations.

The tentative nature of the agreement means final terms are still being worked out between negotiators. Neither the timeline for signing the memorandum nor the exact effective date of the ceasefire extension has been confirmed by US sources.

cards.headline: Trump administration bars Ebola-exposed Americans from returning to US
cards.teaser: Americans exposed to Ebola will be quarantined in Kenya rather than allowed to return to the United States.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is building a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than allowing them to return home. The 50-bed field hospital will open Friday.

Some experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning to the US could hinder treatment efforts for the outbreak.

cards.headline: Justice Department investigates Reid Hoffman nonprofit over E. Jean Carroll case funding
cards.teaser: The DOJ is probing the nonprofit of LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, which helped fund E. Jean Carroll's lawsuit against President Trump.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice is investigating Reid Hoffman's nonprofit organization regarding contributions used to fund E. Jean Carroll's civil lawsuit against President Trump.

The investigation centers on whether Carroll accurately disclosed the funding she received for her legal expenses. Hoffman, a LinkedIn co-founder and major Democratic donor, has been a vocal Trump critic.

cards.headline: Police respond to swatting call at Justice Amy Coney Barrett's home
cards.teaser: Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was targeted in a false emergency call at her Virginia residence.
cards.body:
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett was the victim of a swatting call at her Virginia home. Police radio traffic shows law enforcement received a call for a suspicious noise of gunshots at Barrett's suburban Virginia address.

The dispatcher warned responding officers shortly afterward that a high priority resident of the county lived at the location and that the report may not be authentic. Swatting involves making false emergency calls to prompt armed police response to a target's home.

cards.headline: White House launches website tracking unauthorized immigrant arrests with space theme
cards.teaser: The administration created a site that uses alien encounter imagery to display arrest data for immigrants living in the US without authorization.
cards.body:
The White House launched a space-themed website displaying arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the United States. The site features a Star Wars-style opening crawl and uses the double meaning of "aliens" to create a playful reference to both science fiction and immigration enforcement.

The website highlights immigration statistics through science fiction imagery, drawing a connection between the term "aliens" as used in extraterrestrial contexts and its application to unauthorized immigrants. The design approach allows the administration to present enforcement data while playing on the cultural association between aliens and government secrecy.

cards.headline: Reality TV star Spencer Pratt emerges as serious contender in Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: Former reality television personality Spencer Pratt has surged from novelty candidate to competitive challenger against Mayor Karen Bass.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles mayoral race has drawn national attention as an unconventional municipal contest. Mayor Karen Bass faces competition from 15 candidates, including former reality TV star Spencer Pratt, whose candidacy has gained unexpected momentum in the race.

Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has criticized Pratt's campaign, comparing his rise to Trump's political ascent and suggesting the candidacy is an attempt to revive a television career rather than a genuine bid for office.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer reverses stance on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Governor Gretchen Whitmer walked back a comment saying she would not run for president in 2028.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer has reversed her earlier statement that she would not run for president in 2028. Whitmer is term-limited after winning two gubernatorial elections in the competitive swing state.

The governor has been considered a potential Democratic candidate for the 2028 presidential race. Her change in position indicates she is leaving open the possibility of pursuing a national campaign.
